re_check_result: Round1 evidence.json (4308 bytes) DOES contain real archaeology (git show 4bc292fc, git log on eea5877b, quoted commit bodies) for EVID-1 and EVID-2. The 'no archaeology markers' concern is not correct for EVID-1/EVID-2 themselves. But round1's own note names three claims it explicitly skipped verifying: Q6 WAL 'last server to close', Q1 ADR-0016/ADR-0008 #529, Q13 lint.mjs 1024-char cap. This round ran archaeology on those skipped claims instead of re-stating EVID-1/EVID-2.

findings.title: DECISIONS-r3 Q6 / ADR-0002 'the last server to close runs the WAL checkpoint' invents a coordination mechanism the cited commit does not have
findings.claim_reopened: DECISIONS-r3.md:12 and docs/v2/adr/0002-single-db-git-distribution.md:46: 'WAL checkpoint: the last server to close runs it, plus a checkpoint on close (v1 939c5ca8). GP8 gets a 4-writer case.'
findings.evidence: git show 939c5ca8 -- src/db-base.ts (in cm-main) shows the only change is: closeDB() now ALWAYS runs db.pragma("wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)") wrapped in try/catch before db.close(), with comment 'Checkpoint WAL before close to prevent contention on restart (#103)'. There is no check for 'is this the last server', no counter, no lock file, no PID registry consulted before checkpointing. Every process that closes the DB attempts the checkpoint unconditionally and silently swallows any failure (comment: '/* WAL may not be active */').
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: 939c5ca8 2026-03-13 'fix: add process lifecycle guard to prevent orphaned MCP servers (#103)' (co-authored Claude Opus 4.6). ORIGINAL_INTENT (quoted commit body): 'Also adds WAL checkpoint on DB close to prevent SQLite lock contention from stale connections.' The commit's actual mechanism is simple and unconditional, not a 'last writer' election. REGRESSION_RISK: if v2's GP8 '4-writer case' design assumes a real last-close election (e.g. only firing checkpoint when a ref count hits zero), that is new, unverified, and unbuilt-for-by-v1 behavior being retrofitted onto a commit that never had it. A TRUNCATE checkpoint typically needs no other active readers/writers to fully succeed; with 4 concurrent servers each unconditionally firing TRUNCATE on their own close, the design must handle partial/no-op checkpoints (the v1 code already does, via the swallowed try/catch) rather than relying on an orchestrated 'last to close' guarantee that was never implemented in v1. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: either (a) rewrite the doc line to say 'every server attempts a WAL checkpoint on its own close, best-effort, failures swallowed (v1 939c5ca8)' matching the real fix, and design GP8's 4-writer case around best-effort/idempotent checkpoints, not an election; or (b) if the owner wants true last-writer election for v2, flag it explicitly as new v2 behavior beyond 939c5ca8, not as something the citation already supports.
findings.fix: Correct DECISIONS-r3.md:12 and ADR-0002:46 to describe the checkpoint as unconditional best-effort on every close (matching 939c5ca8), not 'the last server to close runs it'; re-derive the GP8 4-writer case from that simpler, swallow-on-failure behavior.
